Thanks for sharing. I was just found out about this film and was going to watch soon so it’s eerie to see a piece written about it so soon. I’ve already seen one Sjostrom film – The Scarlet Letter – and I was surprised at how effective it was given its age and fairly terrible Youtube rip.

I wonder how this film influenced MGM going forward? Not sure if anyone knows more about the history but I’m certainly interested.
You should definitely watch Terje Vigen and his magnum opus The Phantom Carriage too at some point.
I didn't forget, it was just a big disappointment to me. Tbf the copy I could find looked awful, but still the whole thing was very underwhelming.
Oh, I see. It's actually my favourite, hahaha.

I'm like a modern day "He". I've often joked to myself if my life was made into a film, Todd Solondz would be perfect, but Victor Sjöström would also capture the pathos of my life. Buster Keaton's deadpan style developed when he noticed the less he reacted, the more people laughed.  Schadenfreude and scapegoating is part and parcel of the human heart. As Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn wrote, the dividing line between good and evil is in the heart of every man. As a mentally ill person, I know too well that it's a fact that we're more likely to be victims of crimes than perpetrators and that the majority of violence is by those without a diagnosable mental illness.

I've had traumatic experiences, (trigger warning - like an older sibling spraining my arm twice in childhood, my father rolling my arm up a car window, being pushed into a ditch by a school bully, having axe cologne sprayed in my mouth, having rocks thrown at my face, and being poisoned with feces snuck into a cinnamon bun. ) Because I'm a gay and disabled person (I have depression and anxiety, and I wouldn't be surprised if I have undiagnosed autism, schizophrenia, or ptsd - I hear voices but that's consistent with depression, and not necessarily proof of mental illness). Now people think I have some devilish inclination towards little kids. I like kids, but not in that way. I'm actually a virgin and would only consider having sex that's consensual and romantic; it's probably never getting crossed off my bucket list. I also never had a friend in about twenty years.

I had a grotesque incident near the beach. Some bratty boy farted on my face thinking that he was clever because I wanted him carnally. He thought it was ironic that he gave me something from his butt. I didn't want him or his farts. I thought don't kids these days now some people are into stuff like that? Some woman on tiktok made thousands selling her farts in jars.  Either I was such a deviant that I'd enjoy it and he didn't care or he thought I was deviant enough to like him, but not be into that strange humiliation. At least some people in the community spoke up. One adult said rotten kids. The kid said he's a creep and an adult said that's what you're being. A nice boy objected to when the boy called me a f****. Some adult saw my frozen anxiety and thought I looked like the Casey Hook shooter, a neurodivergent man who shot up an elementary school. I'm actually into nonviolence and I prefer to turn the other cheek, no pun intended. 

> While I wiII admit to a certain cynicism, the fact is that I’m a naysayer and hatchet man in the fight against vioIence. I pride myseIf in taking a punch and I’II gIadIy take another because I choose to Iive my Iife in the company of Ghandi and King. My concerns are globaI. I reject absoIuteIy revenge, aggression and retaIiation. The foundation of such a method is Iove. - Albert's path from Twin Peaks.

Partially as a result of dealing with bullies my whole life, I'm on disability. People think my job in society is village idiot, like Warren Zevon's Mr. Bad Example. Had I not been into humanist philosophies like Christianity, Buddhism, Taoism, and Stoicism, I could have become one of those fellows with an enemy list and a manifesto. From a Nietzschian perspective I have the philosophy of a slave and a doormat. I try to see myself and others as cracked vesels. If someone gives me hate, I don't always succeed in living up to my philosophy. I could have quite the acid tongue. For example, some people call me s***head because of the aforementioned incident. One person quipped while I was carrying my dog's droppings that I was carrying my next meal. I wanted to say this is your heart, but I thought better of it. In one instance someone yelled f you b I work hard for my money. I thought of yelling back, "she works hard for it honey", from the Donna Summers song. I'm not witty, but I could give as good as I get if I wanted to.

I try to keep Montaigne's words that on the highest throne we all sit on our bottom. He knew we're all fools. I figure, wouldn't you rather be the fool who doesn't knows he's a fool? Recently someone who I was sweet on as a kid was down on his luck. I couldn't look him into his eyes out of shame for behavior from about twenty years back, when I thought being a jacka-- and taking the pi-- was the way to have masculine friendship. He was the nicest guy in my life by far. Then people started spreading gossip. While he initially stood up for me, he must have remembered something bad and started to give me a verbal beating. I thought he was the one person I deserved that from, so I took a lot of insults without giving any comebacks. He was about a foot smaller than me in school, and he's still shorter than me (I'm six foot). Since I liked him and I was behind my years emotionally, I didn't know the difference between positive and negative attention. I think he was homeless. I'd still be willing to let him live with me as a live in aide, but he thinks I'm just another ***** who'd try to take advantage of him or see him as some damsel in distress. But if we were to become acquaintances, if anyone played the dominant role it would be him.
You don't hesitate to bear your soul. It's a good way to get support. I'm sorry you have had so much misfortune. Life isn't fair, but keep reaching out to people.

I love this film. One tantalising tidbit, that may or may not be true, has it that Bela Lugosi appears in it uncredited, his first American movie. He could be among the scientists, or the clowns. However, I haven't picked out anyone I'd swear on, so far...
Yeah, I heard that rumor too. Who knows, could be true. Either way it's a great film.

It's been a while since I've seen it and as I said it was a shit copy but visually it wasn't impressive like Terje Vigen and narratively was too simple unlike The Phantom Carriage. Basically seemed to be mostly scrubbed of his genius, I read somewhere that the ending was changed too, maybe the galaxy brains in Hollywood at work even back in the day.
